title: Docker & Docker Compose for AI Developer Workflows
description: A concise, practical guide for AI developers building and running local-first AI applications. The focus is on containerizing AI services that work on everyday hardware, particularly Mac M-series machines, using tools like Ollama and MLX, without requiring a dedicated GPU or NVIDIA/CUDA setup. Learners move from the reproducibility case for containers, through building lean images for Python AI dependencies, running inference containers with persistent model storage, serving local LLMs with Ollama in Docker, and orchestrating a full multi-service AI stack (LLM server, vector database, API/UI) with Docker Compose.
notes: Elective course. Source outline groups lessons into six modules: Why Docker for AI Developers (15m), Building Images for AI Applications (30m), Running AI Containers Locally (25m), Containerizing Ollama for Local LLM Serving (25m), Orchestrating Multi-Service AI Apps with Docker Compose (40m), Practical Patterns and Next Steps (10m).
lesson_length: Concise micro-lessons, roughly 3-8 minutes (300-600 words) each
learning_objectives: Explain the reproducibility and isolation case for containerizing AI development work
Write a Dockerfile that packages a Python AI service with lean base images and cache-friendly layers
Run AI containers with persistent model storage, live-mounted code, and published ports
Serve a local LLM with the official Ollama Docker image and call it from a Python application
Define and operate a multi-service AI stack (LLM, vector store, API/UI) with Docker Compose
Apply image-size, config, and sharing best practices that keep an AI Docker workflow reproducible for a team
prerequisites: Comfortable running commands in a terminal
Basic Python familiarity (can read and run a simple script)

lessons.title: What is Docker?
objectives: Explain the reproducibility and isolation case for containerizing AI development work
Describe the dependency and environment-drift problems Docker solves for Python AI projects

lessons.title: Containers vs. Virtual Machines
objectives: Contrast containers with virtual machines in terms of isolation, startup time, and resource footprint
Explain why containers are lightweight enough for everyday laptops such as M-series Macs

lessons.title: Docker Architecture
objectives: Identify the roles of the Docker Engine, images, containers, and registries
Trace what happens between typing docker run and a process starting in a container

lessons.title: Installing Docker Desktop
objectives: Install and verify Docker Desktop on macOS (Apple Silicon) or Windows
Confirm a working setup by running a hello-world container

lessons.title: The Local AI Developer Workflow
objectives: Describe the model-to-container-to-shareable-application workflow for local-first AI development
Decide when containerizing a local AI project is worth the added complexity

lessons.title: Choosing the Right Base Image
objectives: Select an appropriate Python base image (slim vs. full vs. Alpine) for an AI service
Explain the tradeoffs of image size against build friction for compiled Python packages

lessons.title: Core Dockerfile Instructions
objectives: Use FROM, WORKDIR, COPY, RUN, ENV, EXPOSE, and CMD to define a working image
Read an existing Dockerfile and predict the image it produces

lessons.title: Managing Python AI Dependencies
objectives: Install large AI packages (torch, transformers, llama-cpp-python) efficiently in a Docker build
Pin dependencies so the image builds reproducibly on any machine

lessons.title: Handling Model Weights
objectives: Compare baking model weights into an image against mounting them at runtime
Choose a weights strategy appropriate to local development versus team sharing

lessons.title: Layer Caching for Fast Rebuilds
objectives: Write a Dockerfile that packages a Python AI service with lean base images and cache-friendly layers
Order Dockerfile instructions so dependency layers are not reinstalled on every code change

lessons.title: Tagging and Sharing Images
objectives: Tag images meaningfully and push them to Docker Hub or a private registry
Explain how a shared image gives teammates an identical runtime environment

lessons.title: Running Containers
objectives: Run containers in interactive and detached modes and name them deliberately
Start, stop, and remove containers as part of a daily development loop

lessons.title: Persisting Models and Data with Volumes
objectives: Run AI containers with persistent model storage, live-mounted code, and published ports
Use named volumes so models and data survive container restarts

lessons.title: Bind Mounts for Live Development
objectives: Mount local source code into a container so changes apply without rebuilding the image
Distinguish bind mounts from named volumes and pick the right one per use case

lessons.title: Publishing Ports
objectives: Publish container ports to expose an inference API or UI to the host machine
Diagnose the common failure of a service listening inside the container but unreachable from the host

lessons.title: Executing Commands and Inspecting Containers
objectives: Debug a running container with docker exec and docker logs
Inspect container state to diagnose why a service is failing or misbehaving

lessons.title: What is Ollama and Why Container It?
objectives: Explain what Ollama does and why it suits local LLM serving on consumer hardware
Weigh the portability and reproducibility gains of running Ollama in a container

lessons.title: Running the Official Ollama Docker Image
objectives: Start the official Ollama Docker image, pull a model, and call its REST API
Verify the server is healthy from the host before wiring an application to it

lessons.title: Persisting the Ollama Model Cache
objectives: Use a named volume so downloaded Ollama models survive container restarts
Avoid re-downloading multi-gigabyte models after every docker run

lessons.title: Choosing Models for Low-Memory Hardware
objectives: Choose a model and quantization level (Q4, Q8) appropriate to 8-16 GB of RAM
Reason about the capability, speed, and memory tradeoffs of smaller quantized models

lessons.title: Calling Ollama from a Python Application
objectives: Serve a local LLM with the official Ollama Docker image and call it from a Python application
Use the ollama Python library and OpenAI-compatible endpoints against a containerized server

lessons.title: Why Docker Compose for AI Stacks?
objectives: Explain the multi-service coordination problem Docker Compose solves for local AI development
Recognize when a project has outgrown single docker run commands

lessons.title: Anatomy of a compose.yaml File
objectives: Read and write the services, networks, volumes, and environment sections of a compose.yaml
Map each Compose concept back to the docker run flags it replaces

lessons.title: Building and Starting the Stack
objectives: Bring a stack up and down with docker compose up --build and docker compose down
Understand what state persists across a down/up cycle and what does not

lessons.title: Docker Networking Between Services
objectives: Explain how Compose services reach each other by service name on a shared network
Configure an application container to talk to Ollama or a vector database by hostname

lessons.title: Environment Variables and .env Files
objectives: Manage API keys and configuration with environment variables and .env files instead of hardcoding
Keep secrets out of images, source control, and logs while varying config per environment

lessons.title: Viewing and Filtering Logs
objectives: Use docker compose logs to observe and filter output across a multi-service stack
Diagnose a failing service by following its logs during startup

lessons.title: Full Stack Walkthrough
objectives: Define and operate a multi-service AI stack (LLM, vector store, API/UI) with Docker Compose
Assemble Ollama, ChromaDB, and a FastAPI or Streamlit front end into one working compose.yaml

lessons.title: Image Size and Build Best Practices
objectives: Apply image-size, config, and sharing best practices that keep an AI Docker workflow reproducible for a team
Use multi-stage builds and .dockerignore to keep AI images lean

lessons.title: Sharing Your Stack with Teammates
objectives: Commit compose.yaml and document volume setup so a teammate can reproduce the stack
Treat the Compose file as the shareable definition of the whole development environment

lessons.title: When to Move Beyond Docker Compose
objectives: Recognize the signals that a workload needs Kubernetes, Cloud Run, or a managed inference platform
Describe how local Compose skills transfer to hosted deployment targets

sequencing_rationale: Sequence follows the authored source outline (docker_ai_workflow_outline.md), which groups 31 lessons into six modules: concepts (why Docker, containers vs. VMs, architecture, install, workflow), building images (base images, Dockerfile, Python AI dependencies, model weights, caching, sharing), running containers (run modes, volumes, bind mounts, ports, exec/logs), Ollama for local LLM serving, Docker Compose orchestration culminating in a full Ollama + ChromaDB + FastAPI/Streamlit stack, and closing best practices. Concepts precede image building because a learner cannot reason about Dockerfiles without the image/container distinction; running containers precedes Ollama so the volume and port mechanics are in place before the LLM-specific application of them; Compose comes last as it composes everything prior. Scope assumptions: the course targets consumer hardware (Mac M-series, 8-16 GB RAM) and deliberately excludes GPU/CUDA passthrough, Kubernetes depth (mentioned only as a next step in the final lesson), and MLX serving (named in the description as ecosystem context only — Ollama is the serving tool taught). Hours estimates mirror the source outline's module timings (15/30/25/25/40/10 minutes).

proposed_competencies.competency_text: The learner can define and operate a multi-service application stack with Docker Compose, including service-name networking, shared volumes, and environment-based configuration.
proposed_competencies.rationale: Module 5 (7 lessons, the largest in the course) teaches Compose orchestration, but D5-S6's two competencies cover only the image/container distinction and the decision to containerize — nothing expresses multi-service composition.

proposed_competencies.competency_text: The learner can write a Dockerfile that produces a lean, cache-efficient image for a Python service with heavy dependencies.
proposed_competencies.rationale: Module 2 teaches hands-on Dockerfile authoring (base images, layer ordering, multi-stage builds); D5-S6-C01 is conceptual and does not cover authoring skill.
